correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the all-subset criterion: every leaf must be selected because its incident edge requires that vertex as an endpoint; projecting selected vertices onto the unique n-cycle forces all attachment roots A. A cycle edge lies on every shortest path of some selected pair precisely when every successive positive selected-root gap is <= m=floor((n-1)/2); longer/equal half-cycle gaps cannot be uniquely shortest. Each off-cycle bridge then lies on the unique path from its away-side selected leaf to a selected vertex at another cycle root. This proves the iff condition for all finite connected simple unweighted unicyclic graphs. For an attachment gap d, j additional cycle vertices split it into j+1 positive parts <=m, counted by [t^d](t+...+t^m)^(j+1); multiplication across fixed gaps and arbitrary interior nonleaf choices proves z^ell (1+z)^(N-n-ell+|A|)*prod R_d,m(z). For a bare cycle each k-set appears k times among n marked-start compositions, giving (n/k)*c_m(n,k). Minimum-size coefficients follow from minimal number ceil(d/m) of pieces. Independently enumerated all subsets on 30 small test graphs and got the predicted polynomial; this is bounded corroboration, not proof for all n.
